selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is presented as the beginning of every good thing in this passage?
questions.answer: Starting with the name of Allah.

questions.question: What unusual idea is given about all beings and this phrase?
questions.answer: The passage says creation points to it through its natural state and behavior.

questions.question: Why is the story set in Arabia’s desert instead of in an easy place?
questions.answer: To highlight how serious danger and need can be.

questions.question: What happened to the humble traveler when he faced robbers or came to tents?
questions.answer: He was protected from harm and treated with respect.

questions.question: How did the second traveler’s attitude affect his experience?
questions.answer: His arrogance led to fear, hardship, and shame.

questions.question: What does the passage want the reader to understand about worldly life through this example?
questions.answer: Worldly life is difficult and full of needs, so no one should feel self-sufficient.

questions.question: According to the passage, what should a person do because needs and enemies are so many?
questions.answer: A person should rely on Allah by beginning with His name.

questions.question: What kind of “treasure” is this phrase said to be?
questions.answer: It is a spiritual treasure that opens the way to power and mercy from Allah.

questions.question: What contrast appears between the two examples in the passage: the travelers and the soldier?
questions.answer: Both show that protection and confidence come from acting under rightful authority, not from isolated pride.

questions.question: What main message does the whole passage teach about saying the name of Allah?
questions.answer: It teaches that beginning with Allah’s name brings help, dignity, safety, and a proper relationship with His blessings.

questions.question: What central phrase is the focus of this passage?
questions.answer: The phrase that means beginning in the name of Allah.

questions.question: How does the passage connect this phrase to Muslim identity?
questions.answer: It presents it as a sign that marks Islam.

questions.question: What problem does the desert story help explain?
questions.answer: It explains why human beings need protection and support beyond themselves.

questions.question: How did humility help the first man in practical ways?
questions.answer: It led him to seek protection properly, and that kept him safe and honored.

questions.question: What inner quality caused the other traveler’s trouble?
questions.answer: His pride.

questions.question: Why is the human self called poor and powerless in the passage?
questions.answer: Because it lacks the ability to meet all its needs or defeat all its problems alone.

questions.question: What does taking Allah’s name save a person from, according to the passage?
questions.answer: It saves a person from fearing everything and from begging before creation.

questions.question: How does the phrase transform weakness and need?
questions.answer: It turns them into a way of seeking mercy from Allah.

questions.question: How does the army example show freedom from fear?
questions.answer: A person under official authority is not terrified of everyone around him.

questions.question: What is one major warning found in this passage?
questions.answer: Pride and self-reliance lead to weakness and humiliation, while reliance on Allah leads to safety.

questions.question: According to the passage, what should Muslims begin with when doing something good?
questions.answer: They should begin with the name of Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage say this phrase gives a person?
questions.answer: Great strength and a lasting source of blessing.

questions.question: What statement at the beginning gives the main idea of the passage?
questions.answer: That every good matter should begin with the name of Allah.

questions.question: What phrase does the passage say should come first in good actions?
questions.answer: The name of Allah.
